whatItIs.text: Dried berries of a vine, harvested at different stages: black from cooked-and-dried unripe fruit, white from ripe seeds alone, green from unripe; the heat is piperine, unrelated to chilli capsaicin.

historyNote.text: Native to South Asia and traded since antiquity, black pepper is one of the most commonly traded spices in the world; the word 'pepper' only spread to the unrelated chilli in the 16th century.

howToChoose.text: Buy whole peppercorns and grind fresh — pre-ground pepper loses its aroma in months; the corns should feel heavy and smell sharp when crushed.

storage.text: Keep whole in an airtight tin away from heat and light.

foodSafetyRef.note: Practice storage guidance only; no rulebook content is claimed. The app's food-safety rules live in data/food-safety/rules.json.

useItUp.text: Old peppercorns still work cracked into marinades, pepper sauce, or bloomed in butter; a coarse grind in the mill may just taste tamer.

substitutions.note: same vine, fermented flavour; invisible in cream sauces
fresher, gentler; classic in steak au poivre
